key_insight: DreamLite demonstrates that a unified diffusion model with only 0.39B parameters can run on-device and perform both text-to-image generation and text-guided image editing with competitive quality and low latency.
problem_solved: Large diffusion models (billions of parameters) are costly to run and hard to deploy on-device; existing lightweight on-device diffusion work focuses on generation only and lacks unified support for editing.
method: Design a compact unified diffusion architecture (0.39B) that shares latent representations and conditioning pathways to handle both T2I generation and text-guided image editing.
Apply on-device optimizations (parameter-efficient blocks, architecture-level efficiency, and deployment-aware training) to reduce memory, compute and latency while preserving image quality.
Train with joint objectives and multimodal conditioning so the single model can switch between pure generation and editing tasks using textual prompts plus image-conditioning signals.
impact: Enables practical, private, low-latency image generation and editing directly on consumer devices, lowering deployment cost and expanding real-world use cases for multimodal apps and edge AI.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram comparing unified DreamLite workflow for T2I and text-guided editing (single model, shared latent, different conditioning inputs).
Bar chart or scatterplot: model size (parameters) vs latency vs image quality, highlighting DreamLite at 0.39B with low latency and competitive quality.
Before/after image grid showing example text-guided edits (input photo + prompt → edited output) alongside pure T2I generations.
Icon set illustrating on-device benefits: privacy shield, low-latency stopwatch, small memory chip, and single-model versatility.
paper_title: DreamLite: A Lightweight On-Device Unified Model for Image Generation and Editing
paper_authors: Kailai Feng, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Yang Pan, Hu Ye
